title: Content
description: The content interface: octets to document and back, for one or more content types. This is the entire content of the rule that the kernel knows nothing about JSON — a shape applies to what a content component decoded, never to a guess (shape spec §2.2). See spec.md §6.

embedded.description: On the request the engine repeats after this component asked for embedded content (spec.md §6.6, ADR 0103): what the session's content registry made of each slot it asked for, by the id it gave each. Absent on the first request.

document.description: The decoded document, in the shape language's value model (shape spec §2.1) — JSON values plus bytes. The shape applies to this.

encoded.description: How to read 'document'. Absent means the natural JSON value; 'base64' means octets, for content that decodes to a byte string rather than to structure.

degradations.description: Value-dependent distinctions this decode could not preserve, each with the path where the loss occurred (spec.md §6.4). Static ones are declared in the handshake instead.

embedded.description: Content of another type inside these octets, such as a multipart part's body, which this component asks the engine to decode through the session's content registry before it answers (spec.md §6.6, ADR 0103). A result that carries any is a question, not an answer: the engine does not read its 'document', which the component writes as null, and repeats the request with 'embedded' answered. A component asks once per request, and only of an engine whose handshake declared the 'embedded-content' capability.

Encode.title: Encode
Encode.description: Decode's inverse, and how a selected variant's document becomes the octets a mock serves. decode(encode(d)) must equal d (spec.md §6.2).

shape.description: The shape the document was produced from, as the interaction declares it for the slot, in the form content/compile is given it: present when the engine produced the document from a shape (a mock's reply, a verifier's request), absent otherwise. A component writes from it only what the document cannot say, such as a CSV header for a document with no rows; it never changes what the document is, and decode(encode(d)) must still equal d (spec.md §6.2, ADR 0101).

embedded.description: On the request the engine repeats after this component asked for embedded content (spec.md §6.6, ADR 0103): what the session's content registry wrote of each document it asked for, by the id it gave each. Absent on the first request.

Documents of another type inside this one, such as a multipart part's body, which this component asks the engine to encode through the session's content registry before it answers (spec.md §6.6, ADR 0103). A result that carries any is a question: the engine does not read its 'value', which the component writes as '{ "content": null }', and repeats the request with 'embedded' answered.

EmbeddedDecode.title: EmbeddedDecode
EmbeddedDecode.description: Octets of another type inside a slot's, which a component asks the engine to decode (spec.md §6.6).

id.description: The component's own name for it, unique within one result. The answer comes back under it.

content-type.description: The type the octets are decoded as, routed as a slot's declared type is (spec.md §6.3).

EmbeddedDecodeAnswer.title: EmbeddedDecodeAnswer
EmbeddedDecodeAnswer.description: What the registry made of one embedded slot: the DecodeResult of the component that handles its type, the octets themselves ('encoded: base64') when no component claims it, or 'error' when its component refused the octets, failed, or the content is embedded too deeply (spec.md §6.6). What an error means for the document is the asking component's to say: the multipart component leaves the part's body out.

degradations.description: The losses the decode reported, located in the embedded document. The asking component reports them as its own, located where it put the document (spec.md §6.4).

error.description: Present instead of 'document' when the slot could not be decoded.

EmbeddedEncode.title: EmbeddedEncode
EmbeddedEncode.description: A document of another type inside the one a component is encoding, which it asks the engine to encode (spec.md §6.6).

id.description: The component's own name for it, unique within one result. The answer comes back under it.

at.description: Where the document sits in the one being encoded, as a JSON pointer (RFC 6901). When the request had a 'shape', the engine encodes the embedded document with the part of that shape describing the value there, found through objects, arrays and the modifiers that wrap them, and with none where no one part does.

EmbeddedEncodeAnswer.title: EmbeddedEncodeAnswer
EmbeddedEncodeAnswer.description: What the registry wrote of one embedded document: the EncodeResult of the component that handles its type, or 'error'. Octets need no component and are answered as they are (spec.md §6.6).

error.description: Present instead of 'value' when the document could not be encoded: 'unsupported-content-type' when no component writes its type.

shape.description: The slot's shape document, owned by design 2.2.

path.description: Where the slot is, as a plan path ('$.response.body'), for the component's messages.

CompileResult.title: CompileResult
CompileResult.description: Success: the component can carry the slot's shape under this content type, and the engine compiles the slot (spec.md §6.3). A component that cannot answers with an error, which the engine reports as compile-failed.

fragment.description: Deprecated and ignored: a component contributes no plan (ADR 0100), and says what a value operator means for its type with its handshake's substitutions. It was a plan node in design 2.4's grammar that replaces the engine's generic plan for this slot. It may use the core actions of the grammar it declares, this component's own contributed actions, and resolve paths inside this slot, and nothing else. Returning nothing is legitimate and always safe: the kernel then compiles the slot generically and calls decode at execution time (spec.md §6.3).

grammar-version.description: Deprecated and ignored, with fragment (ADR 0100). It was the plan-grammar version the fragment was authored against: 'v<major>' or 'v<major>.<minor>'. Required whenever a fragment is returned — a fragment without one cannot be checked for skew and is refused. An engine reads it when it has the same major and a minor at least as new; otherwise it fails naming the skew, and never silently reinterprets (spec.md §12.3).

Detect.title: Detect
Detect.description: Do these octets look like a type you handle? For the shape language's content-type operator, the one operator that inspects octets (shape spec §4.2). Optional; used to resolve an absent content type, never to override a declared one (spec.md §6.5).

Label.title: Label
Label.description: What does the document 'decode' makes of 'value' under 'content-type' label the member at 'at' with? For the shape language's content-type operator on a member of a slot's document: a multipart part's body is labelled by the part's own Content-Type (spec.md §6.5, ADR 0077). Optional; a component whose documents carry no labels of their own answers operation-unsupported.

content-type.description: The slot's type, as 'decode' is given it.

at.description: A JSON pointer (RFC 6901) to the member, in the document 'decode' makes of 'value'.

media-type.description: The member's own type. Absent when it carries none, and the engine then detects one from the member as it stands.
